_note: Seeded memory for the ON arm. project 'RUN' means the run's own repo copy (so the primer's project filter matches); any other value is a different project (noise). ts is the backdated write time. Everything here can also be learned by reading the fixture repo; nothing is a secret answer. The two invoice-number decisions are worded without digits on purpose: Termpolis refuses to let one memory supersede another when their numbers differ.

memories.content: ledgerly layout: business logic lives in src/services/*, HTTP handlers in src/routes/handlers/* and they are registered in the ROUTES table in src/routes/index.js, persistence is src/db (store.js plus migrations), shared helpers are in src/lib. src/legacy is dead code from the old monolith billing app: never import it or copy patterns from it (lint rejects imports from it).

ledgerly money rule: amounts are integer cents everywhere. Percentages go through percentOf / basisPointsOf in src/lib/money.js, which use banker's rounding (roundHalfEven). Never use Math.round or .toFixed on money; lint rejects toFixed.

To display money in ledgerly use formatCents(cents, currency) from src/lib/money.js. Customers carry a currency field (USD by default) and anything shown for a customer must use that customer's own currency, e.g. CAD renders with the CA$ symbol.

ledgerly errors: throw new AppError('ERR_SOMETHING') from src/lib/errors.js. Every code must first be registered in src/lib/errorCodes.js with its HTTP status: 400 malformed request, 404 missing resource, 409 state conflict, 422 business rule broken. An unregistered code throws when constructed. The route layer turns an AppError into a { error: code, message } body with that status.

Past fix: a ledgerly test failing with ERR_LEDGER_CLOCK means that test file never froze the clock. Fix it by adding const { useFrozenClock } = require('./helpers/clock') and calling useFrozenClock() at the top of the test file (test/helpers/clock.js). Do not loosen src/lib/clock.js, test/run.js or the harness: clock.js throwing when unfrozen under test is deliberate.

ledgerly schema changes: add a new src/db/migrations/NNN_name.js exporting { id, up(store) }, add it by hand to the MIGRATIONS array in src/db/migrations/index.js (there is no auto-discovery), and bump SCHEMA_VERSION in src/db/schema.js to match. If the migration count and SCHEMA_VERSION disagree, every openStore() throws 'schema drift'. up() must backfill existing rows.
Decision: ledgerly invoice numbers use the global format INV-YYYY-NNNN, one shared sequence for all tenants that resets every January, as produced by the billing module.

Decision: ledgerly invoice numbers no longer use the global INV-YYYY-NNNN format with one shared sequence for all tenants; they now use the per-tenant TENANT_CODE-NNNNNN format, one sequence per tenant in store.tables.sequences, zero-padded to six digits, never reset.
The ledgerly invoice-number format is defined in docs/adr/0007-tenant-invoice-prefixes.md. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and src/legacy/billing.js still describe the older ADR-0004 format and are stale.

A ledgerly route handler has the shape (store, params, body) => { status, body }. Register it as its own [method, pattern, handler] entry in ROUTES in src/routes/index.js; :name segments become params. Handlers stay thin and call a service.

Anything about what is still owed goes through src/services/ledger.js: outstandingFor(store, customerId) for a customer and invoiceOutstanding(store, invoiceId) for one invoice. Do not recompute balances in handlers or other services.

ledgerly not-found: services throw new AppError('ERR_NOT_FOUND') (getCustomer and getInvoice already do), and the router answers 404 with body { error: 'ERR_NOT_FOUND', message }. Calling the service getter is enough to get the standard 404.

ledgerly tests are plain node files named test/*.unit.js using the tiny harness in test/harness.js (test, beforeEach, node assert). npm test runs test/run.js, which picks up every *.unit.js file. No jest or vitest. Shared fixtures: test/helpers/fixtures.js (freshStore, seedCustomers).
ledgerly: no console output in src/, use log from src/lib/logger.js. npm run lint (scripts/lint.js) fails on console calls, on .toFixed, and on imports from src/legacy.
ledgerly dates are UTC, days as YYYY-MM-DD strings, helpers in src/lib/dates.js. The current time comes only from src/lib/clock.js, never new Date() or Date.now() inside src/.

store.tables.sequences is a Map that already exists in every ledgerly store (created by the init migration). Key is the tenant code, value is the last invoice number issued for that tenant. No migration is needed to use it.

ledgerly payments: recordPayment in src/services/payments.js runs inside withTransaction, so a throw leaves the store untouched. Business-rule rejections there are 422 AppErrors with their own registered code, like ERR_CREDIT_LIMIT and ERR_CURRENCY_MISMATCH.

ledgerly invoices: lines are { description, amountCents, type? } and totalCents is sumCents of the line amounts, computed in createInvoice in src/services/invoices.js. Treat invoice objects as values: a function that transforms an invoice returns a new object, because store rows are shared references.
Session note: renamed the customer credit field to creditLimitCents across ledgerly services and fixtures; tests were updated and pass.
Session note: looked at the ledgerly tax-rate loader (src/services/taxes.js reads config/tax-rates.json); nothing changed.
harbor-api: all endpoints return snake_case JSON and paginate with cursor tokens, never offsets.
harbor-api migrations are generated with the ORM CLI and must never be edited by hand after merge.
harbor-api integration tests need the docker compose database up; unit tests do not.
pixelforge: colours come from the design tokens file only; no hex literals in components.
pixelforge builds with vite; the canvas renderer is in src/render and runs in a web worker.
pixelforge: the export dialog froze on huge images because it encoded on the main thread; moved encoding into the worker.
orbit-cli: every command prints machine-readable JSON with --json and human text otherwise; exit code 2 means bad usage.
orbit-cli releases are cut by pushing a tag; the changelog is generated from conventional commit messages.
orbit-cli billing report rounds currency with Math.round because it only displays estimates.
harbor-api errors use RFC 7807 problem+json bodies with a type URI per error.
